enrichment.headline: Adds $7,800 for dock leveler brush seals at Nutrition Services with Commercial Door Solutions
enrichment.summary: The district is adding $7,800 to its agreement with Commercial Door Solutions of Napa, which is installing brush seals on dock levelers and door frames for the Nutrition Services Department. The agreement's cap rises from $16,600 to $24,400. The term is unchanged, December 12, 2024 through June 30, 2025, and the Board is being asked to ratify the change.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2024-2025 - Commercial Door Solutions - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Adds $136,000 for Brigaid to coach cafeteria staff in scratch cooking at the central kitchen
enrichment.summary: The district is adding $136,000 to its agreement with Brigaid LLC of Middletown, CT, which provides coaching and hands-on culinary training for Nutrition Services staff. The training aims to expand scratch cooking and get the Central Production Kitchen's large-batch cook-chill line and cold prep areas fully running. The cap rises from $114,000 to $250,000 and the term stays January 1 through June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2024-2025 - Brigaid, LLC - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Adds $326,840 to buy more chicken wings and chicken strips from Foster Farms for school meals
enrichment.summary: The district is adding $326,840 to its award to Foster Farms, LLC for chicken wings and grilled chicken strips used in K-12 meals, which came out of a competitive request for proposals. The cap rises from $273,160 to $600,000 to buy additional product. The term is unchanged, July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Award - RFP #24-151NS (In Part) - Specialty Proteins K-12 Meal Program For Nutrition Services - Foster Farms, LLC - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Adds $450,000 to buy more fresh fruits and vegetables from Pacific Rim Produce
enrichment.summary: The district is adding $450,000 to its agreement with Pacific Rim Produce of Alameda for fresh fruits and vegetables. The cap rises from $1,900,000 to $2,350,000 to cover additional products. The term is unchanged, July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025, and this is the first renewal option.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 2, Agreement for Fresh Fruits and Vegetables - Pacific Rim Produce - Nutrition Services Department

enrichment.headline: Awards Tulum $312,009 for paving and play-area repairs at Jefferson Child Development Center
enrichment.summary: Tulum Innovative Engineering of Oakland will replace asphalt, damaged play matting and roof eaves at the Jefferson Child Development Center for $312,009, which includes a $35,000 contingency. Tulum was the lowest responsive bidder. Work is expected to start June 5, 2025 and finish within 60 days, by August 5, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor - Tulum Innovative Engineering, Inc. - Jefferson Child Development Center Site Improvements Project - Buildings & Grounds Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies $1,475 for B SAFE to test and inspect playground equipment at Burbank Child Development Center
enrichment.summary: B SAFE Playground Inspection Services of Sunland will do impact testing and inspections of playground structures at the Burbank Child Development Center for a lump sum of $1,475. Work began April 24, 2025 and is expected to last until June 30, 2025. The Board is being asked to ratify the agreement.

vendor.name: B SAFE Playground Inspection Services, Inc.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: General Services Agreement – B SAFE Playground Inspection Services, Inc. – Sites Improvement Project at Burbank Child Development Center - Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Approves Alameda County collecting the district's 2025-26 bond and parcel taxes on property tax bills
enrichment.summary: The district is approving a certification with the County of Alameda that lets the county collect the 2025-2026 bond and parcel taxes, assessments and fees on secured property tax bills on the district's behalf. The text lists no dollar amount.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: 25-Proposition 218 Certification - County of Alameda - Collection of District Bond and Parcel Taxes - Fiscal Year 2025-2026

enrichment.headline: Ratifies $10,000 for MyPath to train 45 teachers and staff in teaching financial literacy
enrichment.summary: MyPath of San Francisco will train 45 district teachers and staff to teach financial literacy, for up to $10,000 between May 15 and December 31, 2025. A separate data-sharing agreement sets the rules for how student data is shared with and protected by MyPath, from September 1, 2024 through December 31, 2025. The Board is being asked to ratify both agreements.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2024-2025 and Data Sharing Agreement - MyPath - High School Linked Learning Office

enrichment.headline: Extends East Bay Art Therapy's contract to June 30, 2025 at the same $37,400
enrichment.summary: East Bay Art Therapy provides art therapy at Dewey Academy, Ralph J Bunche Academy and Street Academy one day a week, and trains students at Dewey to lead peer art sessions. The amendment extends the end date from May 30 to June 30, 2025 without changing the $37,400 amount. The Board is being asked to ratify it.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2024-2025 - East Bay Art Therapy - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Adds $11,000 for Black Cultural Zone summer assemblies for Bridge to Kindergarten and TK students
enrichment.summary: The district is adding $11,000 to its agreement with Black Cultural Zone Community Development for six interactive summer program assemblies and concerts for Bridge to Kindergarten and transitional kindergarten students. The cap rises from $27,820 to $38,820, and the end date moves from June 20 to June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 2, Services Agreement 2024-2025 - Black Cultural Zone Community Development - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Extends Black Cultural Zone's summer podcasting classes to June 30, 2025 at the same $52,690 cap
enrichment.summary: Black Cultural Zone Community Development teaches summer learning podcasting classes after school for 20 students. The amendment moves the end date from May 30 to June 30, 2025 and leaves the $52,690 cap unchanged.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2024-2025 - Black Cultural Zone Community Development - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies $5,000 for National Equity Project to lead equity sessions for Elmhurst United Middle School leaders
enrichment.summary: The National Equity Project will run three to four "Leading for Equity" sessions for school leaders at Elmhurst United Middle School, with follow-up one-on-one sessions for each leader. The sessions focus on shared vision, leadership practices and using an equity lens to manage teams. The cost is up to $5,000 from June 16 to June 30, 2025, and the Board is being asked to ratify it.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2024-2025 - National Equity Project - Elmhurst United Middle School

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $297,000 for Sown to Grow's student well-being check-in platform in all TK-12 schools
enrichment.summary: Sown to Grow of Oakland will provide a platform where students do a weekly social-emotional check-in and wellness survey, plus social-emotional learning lessons, screening, teacher and principal training, coaching and data reports. It would roll out in all TK-12 schools from August 1, 2025 to June 1, 2026 for up to $297,000.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2024-2025 - Sown to Grow - Multi-Tiered Support Systems (MTSS) Department

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $3.6M for the Jewish Community Center of the East Bay to run after-school programs at 3 sites
enrichment.summary: The Jewish Community Center of the East Bay will lead after-school programs at Hintil Kuu Ca Preschool, Joaquin Miller Elementary and Thornhill Elementary, covering homework help, academic support, supervision and enrichment. The master contract runs July 1, 2025 through July 31, 2028 for up to $3,600,000.

vendor.name: Jewish Community Center of the East Bay

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Expanded Learning Programs After School Program Master Contract 2025-2028 - Jewish Community Center of the East Bay - Named Sites - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies $17,848 for International Rescue Committee to help build human trafficking prevention education
enrichment.summary: The International Rescue Committee is one of the required nonprofit partners in a federal Human Trafficking Youth Prevention Education grant. It will work with district staff to build the ability to teach human trafficking prevention to teachers, staff, community members, caregivers and students, from April 1 to June 30, 2025, for up to $17,848. The Board is being asked to ratify it.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2024-2025 - International Rescue Committee (IRC) - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $5.1M for Think Together to run after-school programs at 4 schools through 2028
enrichment.summary: Think Together of Santa Ana will lead after-school programs at Carl B. Munck Elementary, Claremont Middle, Edna Brewer Middle and Montera Middle schools, covering homework help, academic support, supervision and enrichment. The master contract runs July 1, 2025 through July 31, 2028 for up to $5,123,238.99.

items.fundingSource: After School Education and Safety Grant, Expanded Learning Opportunities Program

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Expanded Learning Programs After School Program Master Contract 2025-2028 - Think Together - Named Sites - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies a free pilot of OpenLiteracy reading help for up to 730 students at 27 schools
enrichment.summary: OpenLiteracy of Pittsburgh will pilot its Tier III reading program for up to 730 students at 27 district schools at no cost to the district during 2025-2026. A separate data-sharing agreement covers how student data is shared with and protected by OpenLiteracy for the same term. The Board is being asked to ratify both agreements.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: No Cost Services Agreement and Data Sharing Agreement - OpenLiteracy - Academics and Instruction Department

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $55,000 for The Teaching Well to coach Elementary Network 4 principals and its superintendent
enrichment.summary: The Teaching Well of Oakland will provide twice-monthly executive coaching to the principals and the superintendent of Elementary Network 4, along with leadership coaching. The cost is up to $55,000 for July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2024-2025 - The Teaching Well – Elementary Network 4

enrichment.headline: Ratifies a free Ignite Reading tutoring program for 720 students at 23 schools
enrichment.summary: Ignite Reading of San Francisco will give 720 students at 23 schools 15 minutes a day, five days a week, of one-on-one virtual reading tutoring at no cost to the district, from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. A separate data-sharing agreement covers how student data is shared with and protected by Ignite Reading. The Board is being asked to ratify both agreements.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: No Cost Services Agreement and Data Sharing Agreement - Ignite Reading - Academics and Instruction Department

enrichment.headline: Accepts $11,506 from Oakland Public Education Fund for Skyline music students' Music in the Parks trip
enrichment.summary: The district is accepting an $11,506 grant from the Oakland Public Education Fund to pay for transportation and attendance for Skyline High School music students in the Music in the Parks project. The grant covers April 30 through June 30, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Grant Agreement - Oakland Public Education Fund - Music in the Parks - Skyline High School

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $3,050 for Museum of Children's Art workshops at the Expanded Learning Summer Institute
enrichment.summary: The Museum of Children's Art will work with the district's Extended Learning Office team to develop and lead workshops based on state visual art standards and the theme of the Expanded Learning Summer Institute. The cost is up to $3,050 from July 3 through July 31, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement - Museum of Children's Art - After School Program - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $11,725 for Be the Change Consulting to train after-school program staff
enrichment.summary: Be the Change Consulting of Oakland will work with the Extended Learning Office team to design and run training sessions based on California Department of Education after-school quality standards. The cost is up to $11,725 from July 2 through July 31, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement - Be the Change Consulting - After School Program - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Ratifies McCormick Barstow as outside counsel for up to $110,000 a year through June 2028
enrichment.summary: McCormick Barstow Law Firm will provide legal services for civil lawsuits and other matters as the Legal Department requests, for up to $110,000 per fiscal year from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2028. The agreement is a memorandum of understanding and engagement policy. A data-sharing agreement covers how student data is shared with and protected by the firm.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Memorandum of Understanding and Engagement Policy and Data Sharing Agreement - McCormick Barstow Law Firm - General Counsel

enrichment.headline: Updates the Lafayette Elementary campus ground lease with Kipp Bridge Charter School
enrichment.summary: The district is approving a second amended ground lease and joint use agreement with Kipp Bridge Charter School for the Lafayette Elementary School campus. It adds a legal description of the property, reflects boundaries changed by the 2021 property exchange with the City, and clarifies the initial rent credit. The text lists no dollar amount.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 2, Ground Lease - Joint Use Agreement - Kipp Bridge Charter School - @ LaFayette Elementary School Campus

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $6.8M for Girls, Inc. of Alameda County to run after-school programs at 5 schools
enrichment.summary: Girls, Inc. of Alameda County will lead after-school programs at Allendale Elementary, Bella Vista Elementary, Bridges Academy, Burkhalter Elementary and Horace Man Elementary, covering homework help, academic support, supervision and enrichment. The master contract runs July 1, 2025 through July 31, 2028 for up to $6,789,181.95.

items.fundingSource: After School Education and Safety Grant, Expanded Learning Opportunities Program

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Expanded Learning Programs After School Program Master Contract 2025-2028 - Girls, Inc. of Alameda County - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Adds about $14,700 for ACC Environmental to survey Maxwell Park classroom building for asbestos and lead
enrichment.summary: ACC Environmental Consultants will survey the MLA at Maxwell Park campus new classroom building for asbestos and lead before renovation. The amendment adds money and extends the end date from June 30, 2025 to June 30, 2028 (1,096 more days).

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement – ACC Environmental Consultants, Inc. – MLA at Maxwell Park Campus New Classroom Bldg. Modernization Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Awards Deco Tech Systems $56,948 to install door intercom systems at 4 schools
enrichment.summary: Deco Tech Systems of Walnut Creek will install door entry intercom systems at Allendale Elementary, Sequoia Elementary, Montclair Elementary and Roosevelt Middle schools for $56,948.46, which includes a $5,176.77 contingency. Deco Tech was the lowest responsive, responsible bidder. Work is expected to start June 5, 2025 and finish within 90 days, by September 3, 2025.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – Deco Tech Systems, Inc. – Various Sites Door Entry Systems Upgrades Group 3 Project- Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Approves $57,288 for Geo-Engineering Solutions to study soil for solar projects at 5 school sites
enrichment.summary: Geo-Engineering Solutions of San Ramon will provide geotechnical (soil and ground) consulting for the Solar Photovoltaics Phase 2 and 3 project at Horace Mann Elementary, Oakland Academy of Knowledge, Madison Park Academy, Stonehurst Elementary and Laurel Child Development Center. The $57,288 includes a $5,208 contingency for additional services. Work runs June 5, 2025 to April 30, 2026.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Agreement for Engineering Services – Geo-Engineering Solutions, Inc. – Solar Photovoltaics Phase 2 & 3 Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management - Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.headline: Adds $68.4M for Overaa to build Phase III of the Roosevelt Middle School modernization
enrichment.summary: The district is adding $68,397,205 to its lease-leaseback construction contract with C. Overaa & Company, setting the Guaranteed Maximum Price for Phase III of the Roosevelt Middle School modernization. The cap rises from $7,014,345 to $75,411,550 and the end date moves from July 31, 2027 to September 30, 2029. The text says the amendment is within the Board-approved project budget.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
items.title: Amendment No. 3, Award of a Lease-Leaseback Contract – C. Overaa & Company – Roosevelt Middle School Modernization Project– Division of Facilities Planning and Management

enrichment.summary: Tulum Innovative Engineering will remove and relocate the staff parking lot, a rolling gate pedestal and access control systems for the Cole Data Center Move Project. The district is adding $6,845.70, raising the cap from $36,507.74 to $43,353.44, and extending the end date from July 31 to December 31, 2025 (153 more days).

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
